fieldissues.issue: The title claims $2.7 billion in frozen funding, while the latest description specifies more than $2.2 billion in grants and $60 million in contracts.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Administration Freezes More Than $2.2 Billion in Harvard Grants and $60 Million in Contracts

evidencebasis: The latest descriptions and retained Justice Department, AP, and Harvard sources identify more than $2.2 billion in grants and $60 million in contracts. The title’s $2.7 billion total is inconsistent with those figures.
notes: The medium and long distinguish the freeze from the later court challenge and use the supported amounts.

fieldissues.issue: The title says the administration threatened deportation of protesters, while the latest description and retained Reuters report describe visa revocations and plans for further visa actions.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Administration Revokes Student Visas of Pro-Palestinian Activists

evidencebasis: The Reuters report and latest descriptions identify visa revocations and Rubio’s statement that more actions would follow. They do not describe a general deportation threat against all protesters.
notes: The medium and long attribute the policy rationale and criticism, and the source URL is retained.

fieldissues.issue: The final sentence instructs an editor to describe the event instead of informing readers.
The long repeats instructions about how the event should be understood and uses source-process phrasing about supplied information.
Pam Bondi is tagged but is not named in the assigned packet or latest descriptions.

proposedchanges.description_medium: Remove the final sentence beginning “The event should be described.” The first sentence already identifies the filing and its argument.
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the final source-audit paragraph beginning “The supplied information says.” End with the fact that the request remained pending and depended on the Court’s treatment.

evidencebasis: The Reuters URL and assigned correction identify a March 2025 Supreme Court filing, not an executive order. The latest text states the corrected event but retains editorial instructions; it does not mention Bondi.
notes: The title, category, organization tags, and subject tags fit the litigation event.

fieldissues.issue: “Erases All Federal Transgender Protections” claims a broader result than the described order, which changed federal definitions and rescinded specified directives.
The long says the supplied account describes the order’s effects and then repeats what the White House text confirms, which reads like an audit note.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Signs Order Directing Federal Agencies to Recognize Only Two Sexes
proposedchanges.description_long: Replace “The supplied account describes it as ending federal protections” and “The White House’s executive-order text confirms” with a direct description of the order’s stated agency directions and rescinded directives. Do not claim that all federal transgender protections were erased.

evidencebasis: The White House executive-order text supports the binary federal definition, agency directives, and rescission of specified prior directives. The latest title says all protections were erased, while the long identifies a narrower set of changes.
notes: The human-rights category and transgender-rights, gender-identity, order, and passport tags match the described policy.

fieldissues.issue: “Classified Information Theft” presumes theft, while the descriptions present a search and investigation and explicitly say the warrant grounds were not findings of guilt.

evidencebasis: The DOJ remarks, warrant, and property receipts support the search and listed investigative statutes. The latest descriptions distinguish the search from a guilt finding, which conflicts with the current subcategory’s wording.
notes: The title, descriptions, URLs, category, topic tags, people tags, and organizations fit the search event.
